newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Arianespace says considering tie ups.
newsitem.headline: Arianespace says considering tie ups.

text.p: European space group said on Tuesday it was talking with competitors on possible alliances because the small satellite launching market was becoming overcrowded.
Arianespace's chief executive officer Charles Bigot said there would be six or seven satellite launching companies in the next few and that was "too much."
"There is no neccesity of having six to seven firms offering the same service," Bigot told a news conference. Some would disappear or have to merge, he added.
"We are speaking with competitors (for possible alliances) ... to see if the idea is shared," he said.
Bigot declined to give further details: "We speak to everybody," he said.

French interests control 55 percent of Arianespace shares, with space study centre CNES holding 32 percent. Germany has 18.5 percent and Italy 8.11 percent. Other shareholders are mainly within the European Union.
